svg.title: Fig. 194 — The Cotes spiral r·sin 4θ = a and its inverse, the eight-petalled rose
svg.desc: Redrawn from Robert C. Yates, A Handbook on Curves and Their Properties (1947), Fig. 194, page 215. Section: spirals.

g.data-text: The pole O, the axes, and the circle of radius a: the circle of inversion. The curve and its inverse in this circle meet on it.
The axes of the eight petals of the rose r = a sin 4θ are the radii at 22.5° + k·45°: draw them from O to the circle.
On each petal axis the petal reaches the circle (r = ±a): the eight tips 1–8, met in the order of increasing θ.
The rose r = a sin 4θ: eight petals, every one starting and ending at O and reaching the circle at its tip.
The asymptotes of the spiral: lines parallel to the four lines 0°, 45°, 90°, 135° through O, at the distance a/4 on each side (r sin(4θ) = a: near θ = 0 the height r·sin θ tends to a/4).

The spiral r = a / sin 4θ: eight branches. Each lies between two neighbouring directions kπ/4 and (k+1)π/4, comes in along an asymptote, passes through a numbered point on the circle (r = ±a) and leaves along the next asymptote. It is the inverse of the rose.
